jobs.title: Executive Director, Enterprise Program Management Office (PMO)
jobs.description:
At Veracyte, we offer exciting career opportunities for those interested in joining a pioneering team that is committed to transforming cancer care for patients across the globe. Working at Veracyte enables our employees to not only make a meaningful impact on the lives of patients, but to also learn and grow within a purpose driven environment. This is what we call the Veracyte way – it’s about how we work together, guided by our values, to give clinicians the insights they need to help patients make life-changing decisions.

Our Values

We Seek A Better Way: We pursue bold ideas, embrace complexity, and keep pushing forward.
We Make It Happen: We act with urgency, deliver with excellence, and always find a way.
We Are Stronger Together: We engage with empathy, align around what's best for Veracyte, and celebrate as one team.
We Care Deeply: We show up with integrity, kindness, and respect for one another.

The Position

Veracyte is seeking an Executive Director, Enterprise Program Management Office (PMO) to play a central role in helping us fulfill our mission to transform cancer care with breakthrough molecular diagnostics and AI insights for patients and providers worldwide, leveraging our whole transcriptome and whole genome multi-omics platform. Reporting directly to the Chief Development and Technology Officer, this leader will help accelerate Veracyte’s growth, technical capabilities, and expanding product offerings in key cancer indications by strengthening how we advance strategic initiatives from concept through feasibility, development, and launch. This is a highly visible, high-impact role for a collaborative and trusted leader who can build a next-generation Product Development Process (PDP) that brings rigor, speed, accountability, and clear decision-making to our most important work while reflecting Veracyte’s values of innovation, collaboration, and making it happen.

This position is a hybrid role based out of our San Diego office.

What You’ll Do

Transform Veracyte’s Product Development Process (PDP) into a scalable operating model for advancing initiatives from concept through launch.
Lead enterprise portfolio governance, including intake, prioritization, stage gates, sequencing, escalations, and executive trade-off decisions.
Facilitate monthly executive updates that create shared visibility, thoughtful decisions, and timely resolution of risks, dependencies, and blockers.
Lead quarterly capacity planning to align priorities, resources, timelines, and trade-offs.
Own annual program intake process and portfolio alignment accounting for budget, capacity, business value, and strategic fit.
Standardize program cadence, templates, dashboards, decision records, timelines, risk tracking, and action management.
Strengthen timeline reliability, milestone integrity, critical-path focus, and launch excellence
Define portfolio KPIs for velocity, operational readiness, resource use, and value realization
Serve as a trusted partner across Product, R&D, Operations, Bioinformatics, Software, Finance, Quality, Regulatory, Legal, Commercial, and Market Access.
Prepare clear executive and Board communications, including decision briefs, portfolio updates, risk summaries, and program investment landscape.
Build and lead a high-performing PMO team including hiring, career development, best practices, and a clear vision for the function.

Who You Are

Executive-level PMO, product portfolio management (PPM), or product governance leadership in complex, regulated environments.
Deep expertise in product development, stage-gate governance, portfolio prioritization, resource planning, risk management, and launch readiness.
Proven ability to transform fragmented practices into standardized, scalable, data-driven execution systems.
Strong business acumen, with the ability to connect investment, resources, capacity, trade-offs, and ROI.
Exceptional executive communication skills for senior leadership and development teams alike
Independent judgment and influence to surface risks, resolve blockers, clarify decisions, and help teams move forward.
Strategic thinker who can design operating models while diving into details and solving problems when execution requires it.
Passion for building a PMO center of excellence through coaching, upskilling, practical standards, and shared best practices.
Urgency balanced with quality, collaboration, and patient impact, using agile product development methods to improve speed and transparency.
A personable leadership style grounded in clarity, coaching, accountability, humility, and trust.

Preferred Qualifications

13+ years in program management, portfolio management, product development, or related leadership roles, including 8+ years leading teams or enterprise programs.
Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, engineering, business, or related field required; advanced degree, MBA, or program/portfolio certification preferred.
Experience in diagnostics, life sciences, medtech, biotech, pharmaceutical, or other regulated product environments.
Balancing clinical, regulatory, quality, laboratory, tech, and commercial launch dependencies.
Experience integrating PDP, quality management system (QMS), software development lifecycle (SDLC), and portfolio-management tools.
Ability to build governance mechanisms, dashboards, and cadences that improve transparency and decision quality.
Experience with portfolio analytics, scenario planning, capacity modeling, and value-based prioritization.
Experience implementing enterprise project tools, dashboards, and reporting systems as a reliable source of truth.
Change-management experience rolling out new ways of working.
Aptitude with modern AI tools to automate routine work, improve reporting, and increase PMO productivity.

For candidates based in our San Diego office
, the salary range is $264,000 - $293,000.

The final salary offered to a successful candidate will be dependent on several factors that may include but are not limited to years of experience, skillset, geographic location, industry, education, etc. Base pay is one part of the Total Package that is provided to compensate and recognize employees for their work, and this role may be eligible for additional discretionary bonuses/incentives, and restricted stock units.

Pay range

$264,000—$293,000 USD

What We Can Offer You

Veracyte is a growing company that offers significant career opportunities if you are curious, driven, patient-oriented and aspire to help us build a great company. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, and are committed to fostering an inclusive workforce, where diverse backgrounds are represented, engaged, and empowered to drive innovative ideas and decisions. We are thrilled to be recognized as a 2024 Certified™ Great Place to Work® in both the US and Israel - a testament to our dynamic, inclusive, and inspiring workplace where passion meets purpose.

About Veracyte

Veracyte (Nasdaq: VCYT) is a global diagnostics company whose vision is to transform cancer care for patients all over the world. We empower clinicians with the high-value insights they need to guide and assure patients at pivotal moments in the race to diagnose and treat cancer. Our Veracyte Diagnostics Platform delivers high-performing cancer tests that are fueled by broad genomic and clinical data, deep bioinformatic and AI capabilities, and a powerful evidence-generation engine, which ultimately drives durable reimbursement and guideline inclusion for our tests, along with new insights to support continued innovation and pipeline development. What You'll Do

As Program Director, under the direction of the Executive Director, you will provide overall leadership, management, and accountability for the OASAS-funded FORGE program. jobs.description:
Overview

The earliest years of a child’s life create the foundation for lifelong health, learning, and emotional well-being. At Brookdale Hospital, the HealthySteps Program Director has the opportunity to shape that foundation by leading an innovative, evidence-based program that integrates child development and infant mental health expertise directly into pediatric primary care.

The Program Director provides the strategic, clinical, administrative, and operational leadership necessary to ensure that infants, young children, and their families receive coordinated, family-centered, and developmentally appropriate support in pediatric primary care. The Program Director leads a multidisciplinary team and oversees program quality and fidelity, staff development, grant administration, fiscal performance, clinical operations, data and outcomes reporting, and community partnerships.

HealthySteps, a nationally recognized program of ZERO TO THREE, strengthens the traditional pediatric care model by addressing the developmental, behavioral, social-emotional, and family needs that influence a child’s ability to thrive. HealthySteps at Brookdale Hospital is supported by public and private funding and participates in a multisite, statewide initiative funded by the New York State Office of Mental Health to expand and integrate mental health services within pediatric primary care.

Through collaborative leadership and a commitment to health equity, the Program Director advances Brookdale Hospital’s ability to give children and families—particularly those from historically under-served communities—the strongest possible start in life.

Responsibilities

Leadership and Staff Supervision:

Provide administrative and reflective supervision to a multidisciplinary team of seven (7) staff representing varying disciplines and credential levels, as well as assigned interns and volunteers.
Assign and adjust staff responsibilities to promote operational efficiency, appropriate workload distribution, and maximum delivery of HealthySteps services.
Oversee the HealthySteps’ pediatric residency training program, including curriculum development, delivery, and evaluation.
Establish performance expectations, provide ongoing coaching and feedback, and address performance or conduct concerns in collaboration with Human Resources and departmental leadership.

Grant Management

Lead the development, submission, administration, and renewal of public and private grant applications, continuation requests, and related funding proposals.
Serve as the primary program liaison to funding organizations and ensure compliance with grant requirements, deliverables, performance measures, and reporting deadlines.
Prepare and submit accurate and timely program progress, outcome, financial, continuation, and closeout reports.
Maintain appropriate documentation to support grant monitoring, audits, and program reviews.
Identify potential funding opportunities and collaborate with organizational leadership on strategies to promote program sustainability and expansion.

Budget And Fiscal Management

Develop and manage the HealthySteps operating and grant-funded budgets, including personnel, contractual, and program-related expenditures.
Monitor expenditures against approved budgets and grant line items.
Collaborate with Finance and departmental leadership to prepare budget projections, reconcile expenditures, and address anticipated variances.
Recommend budget modifications and reallocations, when necessary, subject to organizational and funder approval.
Ensure responsible stewardship of public and private program funds.

Program Oversight

Provide strategic and operational leadership for the implementation, maintenance, and continued development of the HealthySteps program.
Ensure fidelity to the HealthySteps model, including participation in national reporting, fidelity monitoring, technical assistance, and site self-assessment activities.
Establish, monitor, and evaluate program goals, workflows, performance measures, service-delivery standards, and patient outcomes.
Oversee program evaluation, data collection, data integrity, and clinical documentation standards.
Ensure the timely and accurate submission of departmental, organizational, regulatory, and funder reports.
Ensure program operations comply with applicable federal and state regulations, grant requirements, organizational policies, professional standards, and patient privacy requirements.
Identify opportunities for performance improvement and lead corrective action and quality-improvement initiatives when appropriate.
Collaborate with pediatric providers and other members of the interdisciplinary care team to support coordinated, family-centered, and developmentally appropriate care.

Organizational And Community Collaboration

Coordinate with hospital departments and clinical programs to address the needs of patients, families, program staff, and community partners.
Participate in and lead special projects, hospital-wide initiatives, and cross-departmental activities, including quality improvement and care-coordination initiatives related to maternal and child health.
Represent HealthySteps and Brookdale Hospital at community meetings, coalitions, professional forums, funding meetings, and partnership activities.
Develop and maintain effective relationships with community-based organizations, government agencies, healthcare providers, educational institutions, and other stakeholders.
Advocate for accessible, culturally responsive, trauma-informed services for infants, young children, and their families.
Perform other related duties consistent with the position’s responsibilities and necessary to support the successful implementation and sustainability of the HealthySteps program.

Qualifications

Education:

Master’s Degree in psychology, social work, or counseling from an accredited college or university, required.
Doctoral degree in psychology, counseling, social work, infant mental health or related discipline, preferred.

Experience

Minimum of three (3) years of progressively responsible experience in program administration, clinical program operations, or project management, required.
Minimum of two (2) years of supervisory or management experience, including responsibility for staff development and performance management, required.
Experience working in a healthcare, pediatric, behavioral health, integrated primary care, or community-based clinical setting, preferred.
Experience administering grant-funded programs, including performance monitoring and preparation of grant or funder reports, preferred.
Demonstrated experience working with infants, children under three years of age, parents, caregivers, and families, preferred.
Experience assessing or supporting infant and early childhood growth, development, social-emotional functioning, and parent-child relationships, preferred.

Licenses/Certifications

Current and valid New York State license as a Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) or Licensed Psychologist required.
License must be in good standing and maintained throughout employment with OBH.

New York State Infant Mental Health endorsed, preferred.

Knowledge And Skills

Excellent oral and written communication skills, including grant writing, funder reporting and clinical documentation.
Advanced knowledge of infant and early childhood development, infant mental health, parent-child relationships, family systems, and developmentally appropriate interventions.
Advanced knowledge of reflective supervision principles and the demonstrated ability to apply them in a multidisciplinary clinical environment.
Demonstrated ability to lead, develop, motivate, and evaluate multidisciplinary teams representing different professional disciplines and credential levels.
Knowledge of integrated pediatric primary care, family-centered care, trauma-informed practice, and culturally responsive service delivery.
Ability to interpret grant requirements and translate them into measurable program objectives, workflows, and staff responsibilities.
Ability to collect, analyze, interpret, and report program quality, utilization, and fidelity data.
Working knowledge of budget development, expense monitoring, financial projections, and fiscal reporting.
Strong interpersonal, presentation, facilitation, and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational, analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and respond effectively to changing program needs.
Ability to establish productive working relationships with patients, families, clinical teams, funders, community partners, and organizational leadership.
Demonstrated commitment to serving culturally diverse and medically or economically underserved populations.
Proficiency with electronic health record systems, data-reporting platforms, and standard office productivity software.

Physical Requirements

Position requires prolonged periods of sitting, standing, reaching, and walking throughout the working day.
Position requires travel between main hospital and ambulatory care sites.
Position will be required to stoop, bend, lift, and carry items weighing up to 25 pounds.

Job Description

Are you passionate about shaping financial strategy and promoting impactful change? Join our Treasury team as Executive Director, where you will lead the design and implementation of transfer pricing and funding policies that support our firm's balance sheet and resource allocation goals. This high-visibility role offers the opportunity to collaborate with senior leaders across Treasury, Finance, and Business teams, influencing key decisions and ensuring best-in-class policy frameworks. You will work in a dynamic environment, leveraging your technical expertise and leadership skills to deliver innovative solutions, including exploring how Big Data, AI, and Machine Learning can modernize and enhance traditional FTP and Treasury analytics.

As a Funds Transfer Pricing, Executive Director within the Treasury team, you will oversee the development, implementation, and governance of transfer pricing and funding policies, including Funds Transfer Pricing (FTP), to support the firm's balance sheet strategy and resource allocation. The role requires strong technical skills, a solid understanding of banking products, balance sheets, and ledger structures, and the ability to lead projects and collaborate with senior stakeholders across Treasury, Finance, and Business teams.

Job Responsibilities

Develop and maintain transfer pricing methodologies, including FTP and internal funding frameworks such as marginal funding curves, FTP spread methodologies across currencies, and liquidity premium attribution
Align policies with liquidity premiums, funding spreads, entity and currency considerations, and balance sheet structure
Update methodologies to reflect market conditions, regulatory requirements, and business strategy
Recommend and implement policy changes to support efficient resource allocation and balance sheet management
Oversee analysis of funding consumption, FTP allocations, and resource usage at business and legal entity levels; support scenario modeling and impact analysis including CCAR stress testing forecasts for NII, interest revenue/expense, and non-interest revenue
Prepare reports and presentations on transfer pricing and funding policy impacts for senior management
Ensure accurate mapping and reconciliation of FTP and funding charges within ledger and balance sheet accounts
Lead cross-functional projects to implement new transfer pricing and funding frameworks; govern consistent application of policies and communicate changes across teams
Collaborate with Treasury, Finance, front office, and risk teams to ensure effective policy implementation and stakeholder engagement
Support the full model development lifecycle end-to-end (development, validation, audit, implementation, and governance) and identify opportunities to apply AI/ML/Big Data to improve FTP analytics and liquidity cost attribution
Drive the Transformation Agenda for FTP/funding (target-state design, roadmap, process/data/technology modernization, and adoption) to improve transparency, controls, and scalability

Required Qualifications, Capabilities And Skills

10+ years of experience in treasury, FTP, asset and liability management, or funding management at a financial institution
Strong understanding of banking products such as loans, deposits, derivatives, and securities, as well as balance sheets and ledger structures
Experience with transfer pricing and FTP methodologies, including liquidity and funding frameworks
Strong analytical and quantitative skills; proficiency in Excel, SQL, Python, or similar tools
Experience leading cross-functional projects and managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including experience presenting to senior management and participating in governance forums such as FTP Committees
Detail-oriented, proactive, and committed to continuous improvement, with the ability to synthesize complex information and present it clearly to diverse audiences

Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities And Skills

Advanced degree in Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, Data Science, or related field
Experience with regulatory frameworks such as Basel III/IV, LCR, NSFR, and experience supporting regulatory reviews or engaging directly with regulators (OCC, Fed) on FTP, capital allocation, or liquidity topics
Experience with FTP and liquidity cost allocation for markets trading, securities financing, and derivatives portfolios; familiarity with Initial Margin (IM), Variation Margin (VM), CCP margining processes, and Funding Valuation Adjustment (FVA) frameworks
Exposure to interest rate risk models (VaR/SVaR), Monte Carlo simulation, or ALM platforms (e.g., QRM); experience with model validation and audit processes
Familiarity with data visualization and reporting tools (e.g., Tableau, QlikSense)
Experience working in a large, matrixed financial institution
Experience with or interest in applying Machine Learning, AI, or Big Data tools (e.g., Spark, cloud data platforms) to Treasury analytics, liquidity modeling, or automation

Our impact comes to life through the products we build, in the stories of our customers, and in our growing commitment to land stewardship and recreational access.

ABOUT ACCESS & STEWARDSHIP AT OnX

Access and Stewardship (A&S) is central to onX's mission and long-term relevance in the outdoor industry. Our products help people understand access, navigate land boundaries, and make confident decisions outside. But the future of outdoor recreation is shaped not only by technology, but by the stewardship of the places people use and the policies that determine how lands are accessed, managed, and understood.

onX's A&S program brings these pieces together through charitable giving, stewardship projects, customer education, geospatial storytelling, access-informed tools, and a growing advocacy and government relations practice on issues that affect access, stewardship, and federal geospatial data. This work strengthens customer trust, reinforces onX's role as a credible voice in the outdoor space, and connects our products and expertise to real-world outcomes for public lands and outdoor communities.

About This Opportunity

onX is seeking an experienced Access & Stewardship Program Director to run and grow the company's A&S program. This person defines program priorities, drives annual planning, and oversees grants, stewardship initiatives, customer education, access-related geospatial and product integration projects, partnerships, and policy-informed programs.

The Program Director is both a strategist and a hands-on operator. The core of the job is program strategy, prioritization, and delivery: translating A&S priorities into clear plans and measurable initiatives that align with onX's business and brand priorities. This person connects policy context, stewardship priorities, partnerships, education, and tools into a cohesive program rather than a set of disconnected efforts.

A defining part of this role is guiding how onX expands its political exposure: deliberately, in nonpartisan and credibility-building ways, and with clear-eyed judgment about risk. This person will surface trade-offs and risks early and provide clear recommendations so senior leadership can make deliberate, informed decisions.

Success looks like a focused and credible program, sound partner and investment choices, measurable progress, and executive-ready reporting on impact, trade-offs, and where to invest next. This role reports to the Director of Brand Programs.

What You'll Do

Set Strategy & Own the Program

Qualifications

What You Bring to Cambia:

The Program Director, Provider Partnership would have a bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration or related field (Master’s preferred) and 10+ years of related experience in business or health care management with preference for experience driving transformation programmatic innovation, Alternative Payment Model development, payment innovation and/or strategic implementation or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Skills And Attributes

Alternative Payment Model Leadership: Ability to lead healthcare innovation initiatives with functionally diverse stakeholders across the organization
Strategic Communication: Strong facilitation and consensus-building skills with internal/external teams at all organizational levels
Healthcare Industry Expertise: Knowledge of industry trends, provider relations, and value-based reimbursement methods
Team Leadership: Proven track record managing multi-discipline, high-performance teams and diverse work streams
Project & Resource Management: Competency in budgeting, organizing work, establishing success measures, and managing deliverables
Business Transformation: Experience initiating and managing complex transformation programs and leading organizational change
Business Case Development: Ability to construct actionable business cases and track implementation of new operational processes
Strategic Thinking & Partnership: Big-picture perspective with strong relationship-building skills and collaborative team approach

What You Will Do At Cambia

Uses strong knowledge of department strategies and organizational vision to represent Network Innovations in various forums and provide thought leadership for strategic program development
Leads Alternative Payment Model program development and integration activities including strategy, design, architecture, quality assurance, customer experience, and operational sustainment
Serves as key point of contact with strategic vendors while facilitating operational and strategic interactions with internal and third-party stakeholders
Ensures delivery of sustained program interactions with key customer segments (providers, members, employers) and integration with other value-based programs
Organizes, motivates, and leads program development efforts with functionally and geographically diverse delivery teams across the company
Identifies critical program risks and issues, drives resolution, and ensures requirements and dependencies are communicated to relevant stakeholders
Maintains expertise on industry best practices and value-based healthcare innovation while representing Cambia as a leader at conferences and industry events

Working at Cambia means being part of a purpose-driven, award-winning culture built on trust and innovation anchored in our 100+ year history. Our caring and supportive colleagues are some of the best and brightest in the industry, innovating together toward sustainable, person-focused health care. Whether we're helping members, lending a hand to a colleague or volunteering in our communities, our compassion, empathy and team spirit always shine through.

At Cambia, You Can

Work alongside diverse teams building cutting-edge solutions to transform health care.
Earn a competitive salary and enjoy generous benefits while doing work that changes lives.
Grow your career with a company committed to helping you succeed.
Give back to your community by participating in Cambia-supported outreach programs.
Connect with colleagues who share similar interests and backgrounds through our employee resource groups.

We believe a career at Cambia is more than just a paycheck – and your compensation should be too. Our compensation package includes competitive base pay as well as a market-leading 401(k) with a significant company match, bonus opportunities and more.

Benefits

In exchange for helping members live healthy lives, we offer benefits that empower you to do the same. Just a few highlights include:

Medical, dental and vision coverage for employees and their eligible family members, including mental health benefits.
Annual employer contribution to a health savings account.
Generous paid time off varying by role and tenure in addition to 10 company-paid holidays.
Market-leading retirement plan including a company match on employee 401(k) contributions, with a potential discretionary contribution based on company performance (no vesting period).

Commute and parking benefits.

new_jobs.description:
Overview

The earliest years of a child’s life create the foundation for lifelong health, learning, and emotional well-being. At Brookdale Hospital, the HealthySteps Program Director has the opportunity to shape that foundation by leading an innovative, evidence-based program that integrates child development and infant mental health expertise directly into pediatric primary care.

The Program Director provides the strategic, clinical, administrative, and operational leadership necessary to ensure that infants, young children, and their families receive coordinated, family-centered, and developmentally appropriate support in pediatric primary care. The Program Director leads a multidisciplinary team and oversees program quality and fidelity, staff development, grant administration, fiscal performance, clinical operations, data and outcomes reporting, and community partnerships.

HealthySteps, a nationally recognized program of ZERO TO THREE, strengthens the traditional pediatric care model by addressing the developmental, behavioral, social-emotional, and family needs that influence a child’s ability to thrive. HealthySteps at Brookdale Hospital is supported by public and private funding and participates in a multisite, statewide initiative funded by the New York State Office of Mental Health to expand and integrate mental health services within pediatric primary care.

Through collaborative leadership and a commitment to health equity, the Program Director advances Brookdale Hospital’s ability to give children and families—particularly those from historically under-served communities—the strongest possible start in life.

Responsibilities

Leadership and Staff Supervision:

Provide administrative and reflective supervision to a multidisciplinary team of seven (7) staff representing varying disciplines and credential levels, as well as assigned interns and volunteers.
Assign and adjust staff responsibilities to promote operational efficiency, appropriate workload distribution, and maximum delivery of HealthySteps services.
Oversee the HealthySteps’ pediatric residency training program, including curriculum development, delivery, and evaluation.
Establish performance expectations, provide ongoing coaching and feedback, and address performance or conduct concerns in collaboration with Human Resources and departmental leadership.

Grant Management

Lead the development, submission, administration, and renewal of public and private grant applications, continuation requests, and related funding proposals.
Serve as the primary program liaison to funding organizations and ensure compliance with grant requirements, deliverables, performance measures, and reporting deadlines.
Prepare and submit accurate and timely program progress, outcome, financial, continuation, and closeout reports.
Maintain appropriate documentation to support grant monitoring, audits, and program reviews.
Identify potential funding opportunities and collaborate with organizational leadership on strategies to promote program sustainability and expansion.

Budget And Fiscal Management

Develop and manage the HealthySteps operating and grant-funded budgets, including personnel, contractual, and program-related expenditures.
Monitor expenditures against approved budgets and grant line items.
Collaborate with Finance and departmental leadership to prepare budget projections, reconcile expenditures, and address anticipated variances.
Recommend budget modifications and reallocations, when necessary, subject to organizational and funder approval.
Ensure responsible stewardship of public and private program funds.

Program Oversight

Provide strategic and operational leadership for the implementation, maintenance, and continued development of the HealthySteps program.
Ensure fidelity to the HealthySteps model, including participation in national reporting, fidelity monitoring, technical assistance, and site self-assessment activities.
Establish, monitor, and evaluate program goals, workflows, performance measures, service-delivery standards, and patient outcomes.
Oversee program evaluation, data collection, data integrity, and clinical documentation standards.
Ensure the timely and accurate submission of departmental, organizational, regulatory, and funder reports.
Ensure program operations comply with applicable federal and state regulations, grant requirements, organizational policies, professional standards, and patient privacy requirements.
Identify opportunities for performance improvement and lead corrective action and quality-improvement initiatives when appropriate.
Collaborate with pediatric providers and other members of the interdisciplinary care team to support coordinated, family-centered, and developmentally appropriate care.

Organizational And Community Collaboration

Coordinate with hospital departments and clinical programs to address the needs of patients, families, program staff, and community partners.
Participate in and lead special projects, hospital-wide initiatives, and cross-departmental activities, including quality improvement and care-coordination initiatives related to maternal and child health.
Represent HealthySteps and Brookdale Hospital at community meetings, coalitions, professional forums, funding meetings, and partnership activities.
Develop and maintain effective relationships with community-based organizations, government agencies, healthcare providers, educational institutions, and other stakeholders.
Advocate for accessible, culturally responsive, trauma-informed services for infants, young children, and their families.
Perform other related duties consistent with the position’s responsibilities and necessary to support the successful implementation and sustainability of the HealthySteps program.

Qualifications

Education:

Master’s Degree in psychology, social work, or counseling from an accredited college or university, required.
Doctoral degree in psychology, counseling, social work, infant mental health or related discipline, preferred.

Experience

Minimum of three (3) years of progressively responsible experience in program administration, clinical program operations, or project management, required.
Minimum of two (2) years of supervisory or management experience, including responsibility for staff development and performance management, required.
Experience working in a healthcare, pediatric, behavioral health, integrated primary care, or community-based clinical setting, preferred.
Experience administering grant-funded programs, including performance monitoring and preparation of grant or funder reports, preferred.
Demonstrated experience working with infants, children under three years of age, parents, caregivers, and families, preferred.
Experience assessing or supporting infant and early childhood growth, development, social-emotional functioning, and parent-child relationships, preferred.

Licenses/Certifications

Current and valid New York State license as a Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) or Licensed Psychologist required.
License must be in good standing and maintained throughout employment with OBH.

New York State Infant Mental Health endorsed, preferred.

Knowledge And Skills

Excellent oral and written communication skills, including grant writing, funder reporting and clinical documentation.
Advanced knowledge of infant and early childhood development, infant mental health, parent-child relationships, family systems, and developmentally appropriate interventions.
Advanced knowledge of reflective supervision principles and the demonstrated ability to apply them in a multidisciplinary clinical environment.
Demonstrated ability to lead, develop, motivate, and evaluate multidisciplinary teams representing different professional disciplines and credential levels.
Knowledge of integrated pediatric primary care, family-centered care, trauma-informed practice, and culturally responsive service delivery.
Ability to interpret grant requirements and translate them into measurable program objectives, workflows, and staff responsibilities.
Ability to collect, analyze, interpret, and report program quality, utilization, and fidelity data.
Working knowledge of budget development, expense monitoring, financial projections, and fiscal reporting.
Strong interpersonal, presentation, facilitation, and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational, analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and respond effectively to changing program needs.
Ability to establish productive working relationships with patients, families, clinical teams, funders, community partners, and organizational leadership.
Demonstrated commitment to serving culturally diverse and medically or economically underserved populations.
Proficiency with electronic health record systems, data-reporting platforms, and standard office productivity software.

Physical Requirements

Position requires prolonged periods of sitting, standing, reaching, and walking throughout the working day.
Position requires travel between main hospital and ambulatory care sites.
Position will be required to stoop, bend, lift, and carry items weighing up to 25 pounds.
